questions.q: Why shouldn't a deploy job run every time a pull request is opened against main?
options: Because pull requests are always broken
Because GitHub doesn't allow deploy jobs on pull requests at all
Because you only want to deploy after code is actually merged into main, not just proposed in an open PR
Because deploy jobs can only run on Fridays
questions.explain: An open PR is a proposal, not a merged change — deploying on every PR would ship unreviewed, unmerged code.

questions.q: In `if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`, what does this condition specifically require?
options: Any event at all, on any branch
The workflow must be manually triggered by a human
Only that a pull request exists, regardless of branch
The event must be a push (not a pull_request), AND the branch being pushed to must literally be main
questions.explain: Both conditions must be true: the triggering event is a push, and that push landed specifically on the main branch — which together describe a real merge to main.

questions.q: What does `needs: build-and-test` do for the deploy job?
options: It makes the deploy job wait and only run after the build-and-test job succeeds
It deletes the build-and-test job
It has no functional effect, only cosmetic
It runs build-and-test and deploy simultaneously with no ordering
questions.explain: needs: creates a dependency, ensuring deploy only runs once the referenced job (build-and-test) has completed successfully.

questions.q: Why are GitHub Actions secrets used instead of hardcoding a deploy token directly in the workflow YAML file?
options: Hardcoded values run faster
YAML files cannot contain any text strings at all
Secrets are only cosmetic and provide no real security benefit
Workflow files are plain text visible to anyone who can read the repository; secrets stay encrypted and are masked in logs
questions.explain: A workflow file is plain text in the repository; secrets keep sensitive values out of that plain text and mask them automatically if they ever appear in log output.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does 'deploy' mean for a dbt project, compared to a typical web app?
options: There's no server to restart — successfully running dbt build against the production target IS the deploy
dbt projects can never be deployed via GitHub Actions
It means exactly the same thing as restarting a web server
dbt projects require a separate, unrelated deployment tool entirely
questions.explain: Unlike a web app that might restart a running process, a dbt project's 'deploy' is the successful completion of the build command against production, which directly updates the production tables.
